Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

truce noun

also armistice, ceasefire, cease-fire, the cease-fire is holding, call for a cease-fire, make a truce, break a truce

classical

Cic. Off. 1.33: cum trīgintā diērum essent cum hoste pactae indūtiae (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 186, 188

indūtiae, indūtiārum f. pl.

noun, first declension, plural

a truce, an armistice, a cease-fire

Plural only. Varro called a truce bellī fēriae, a holiday of war (Gell. 1.25.2, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • indūtiās facere

    to make a truceTraupman 188; cf. Cic. Phil. 8.20 (Lewis & Short)

  • indūtiās violāre

    to break a truceTraupman 188

  • indūtiās poscere

    to call for a cease-fireTraupman 186

  • Indūtiae dūrant.

    The cease-fire is holding.Traupman 186

  • indūtiae annōrum sex

    a six years’ truceTraupman 188

See also peace, treaty, war.

SourcesLewis & Short: indutiae

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
